material_finding: The stable distillery entrypoint already wrapped provider secret and network access behind typed FREE admission, but the shared rae_secret_loader primitive itself could still read provider environment variables or repository credential stores when called directly by legacy/base code. This left a defense-in-depth pre-secret ordering gap below the guarded entrypoint. The canonical 8.68 law requires provider admission before secret/key lookup, not merely before the normal supervisor entrypoint.
hypothesis: Moving the provider FREE admission check into the shared credential primitive closes direct/legacy pre-secret reads without weakening non-provider secret behavior and without introducing a second provider authority.
counterhypothesis: Guarding only the stable distillery/swarm entrypoints is sufficient because direct/base secret-loader callers are not part of current execution.
counterhypothesis_adjudication: REJECTED_AS_TOO_WEAK_FOR_CURRENT_INVARIANT: the active supervisor states the boundary as BEFORE_SECRET_OR_KEY_LOOKUP, and the shared loader is itself a lookup primitive. A caller-path assumption cannot substitute for a primitive-level fail-closed guard.

sources.title: Multi-component Causal Tracing in Large Language Models
sources.principle: single-layer/single-component tracing can miss causal subsets; soft multi-component interventions can search sparse impactful sets more efficiently

sources.title: When Chain-of-Thought Fails, the Solution Hides in the Hidden States
sources.principle: activation-patching effects are token- and layer-localized and can reveal recoverable task information not expressed by the visible reasoning trace

sources.title: Hidden Error Awareness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: The Signal Is Diagnostic, Not Causal
sources.principle: high-quality hidden-state readout can remain diagnostic rather than causal; steering/patching failure is a required counterexample to equating decodability with control

sources.title: Steering the Language Axis: From Linear Decodability to Causal Control
sources.principle: causal steering needs matched random-direction controls and layer-specific intervention mapping rather than assuming any decodable direction is a causal lever

jspace_fusion.proposal: JSPACE_VECTOR_CONTROL_ABI/v1 acceptance should separate DIAGNOSTIC_READOUT from CAUSAL_CONTROL and bind every causal promotion to model identity, layer/token/component locus, matched random-direction or equivalent placebo controls, target metric, off-target regressions, and intervention digest.
jspace_fusion.counterevidence_preserved: A hidden representation can predict correctness strongly yet fail all attempted causal interventions; therefore J-Space recurrence, probe AUROC or decodability must not promote a vector to a control primitive.
